question.:question/problem:
$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -7 & -6 \\ 2 & 6 & 4 \\ 6 & 1 & -2\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}43 & 0 & -20 \\ -34 & 0 & 16 \\ 6 & 1 & -2\end{bmatrix}
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_{i}:=R_{i}+kR_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above $a_{32}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}1 & -7 & -6 \\ 2 & 6 & 4 \\ 6 & 1 & -2\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{1}:=R_{1}+7R_{3}}\begin{bmatrix}43 & 0 & -20 \\ 2 & 6 & 4 \\ 6 & 1 & -2\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{2}:=R_{2}-6R_{3}}\begin{bmatrix}43 & 0 & -20 \\ -34 & 0 & 16 \\ 6 & 1 & -2\end{bmatrix}=B
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$R_{1}:=R_{1}+7R_{3}$ and $R_{2}:=R_{2}-6R_{3}$.

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_{i}:=R_{i}+kR_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above $a_{33}=2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}-9 & -7 & -2 \\ -10 & 8 & -8 \\ -5 & 5 & 2\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{1}:=R_{1}+R_{3}}\begin{bmatrix}-14 & -2 & 0 \\ -10 & 8 & -8 \\ -5 & 5 & 2\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{2}:=R_{2}+4R_{3}}\begin{bmatrix}-14 & -2 & 0 \\ -30 & 28 & 0 \\ -5 & 5 & 2\end{bmatrix}=B
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$R_{1}:=R_{1}+R_{3}$ and $R_{2}:=R_{2}+4R_{3}$.
